# Marketplace: state of the business and three decisions

**To:** VP Marketplace · **Data:** Olist public extract, orders 2017-01-01 to 2018-08-31 · **Read time:** 5 min · _Generated by `make results`; every number is in docs/RESULTS.md_

## State of the business
- **Growth has stalled.** GMV has been flat since Nov-2017. Jun–Jul 2018 ran **12.0% below Mar–May** (days 1–20 of Jun–Aug: 11.0%; August capture decays after Aug 21; the World Cup overlaps Jun–Jul). Active sellers 1,072 → 1,206, GMV per seller R$923 → R$722/month: demand is the constraint. "+138% YoY" is a ramp-up base effect.
- **"Late costs ~1.9 stars" is mostly survey timing.** The survey fires 2 days after the promised date, so most late orders are rated before arrival. Same seller, same month: **-1.89★** recorded vs **-0.51★** after delivery (carrier-leg only -0.54★). A truckers'-strike IV confirms the recorded penalty (-1.49★; -1.22 with seller FE).
- **The spring-2018 slump was a carrier-transit tail plus a promise cut.** Late rate Jan → Mar 5.7% → 19.0%: carrier transit +8.1 pp, promise cut +6.0 pp, sellers -1.4 pp.
- **Repurchase is underpowered:** -0.29 pp; MDE 0.66 pp (36% of base).

## Decisions (in priority order)
| # | Decision | Why | Sized impact (12 mo) | Confidence | Owner / date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Split the survey: delivery-issue contact at promise + 2 days, star rating on confirmed delivery** | 70% of late orders are rated before they arrive. | removes ≤ 2,215 pre-delivery 1–2★ ratings/yr (≈1,866 with exact-day matching); value = rating accuracy, no BRL claimed | High on direction, medium on size | CX product manager; ship by 2018-09-30 |
| 2 | **Don't roll out shorter promises; A/B a 3-day-capped lane-P80 after the peak** | Full year, lane-P80 saves 6.4 d but late rises 9.3% → 20.6%. | capped arm: −1.6 d, late 9.3% → 10.8% (full year); pays only above +0.032% conversion per day saved | Low: upside unmeasured | Delivery-promise PM + analytics; run 2019-01-14 → 2019-02-10 (after the peak and after #1), final read-out 2019-03-03 |
| 3 | **Fix partial shipments: mark 'delivered' only when every item has arrived, and announce split shipments** | 'Incomplete order' is a top-two complaint on ON-TIME orders (23%, CI 19%–27%); 65% are multi-item orders (12% of reviews). | ≤ 973 1–2★/yr on R$220k/yr of orders (upper bound); raises the measured late rate | Medium (text classifier, silver labels) | Marketplace ops + order-management engineering; scope by 2018-10-01 |

**A/B (#2):** 50/50 by customer, ≈3,005 orders/arm. Primary: conversion. Guardrail: matured late rate vs control ≤ +3 pp (MDE 1.9 pp). Kill: in-flight past-promise share +3 pp for 3 days. Oct-2017 analog: a 5-day cap was +4.2 pp (would trip), the 3-day cap +2.3 pp. This overrides the pre-set rule (appendix).

**Ask today:** approve #1 and schedule #2. **Deprioritised:** lanes, seller-rating money (appendix).

---
### Appendix: methodology and caveats
- Seller quality plan for the 82 'fix-first' sellers (22% of GMV, 87% on-time): ops hygiene, no measurable BRL.
- Lane/carrier programme: against a lane-adjusted baseline the 10 worst lanes have only 277 excess late orders/yr (≈57 1–2★ recorded, 20 post-delivery), down from 1,143 vs the network average. No carrier ID exists.
- Money on reviews: one extra 1–2★ review is associated with −R$13 of the seller's next-4-week GMV (95% CI −R$62 to R$36): not detectable. Caveat: per the dataset description, Olist sells through the 'Olist Store' on partner marketplaces, so buyers may mostly see the store's reputation rather than a seller's; the seller-week panel may be the wrong unit, so the null is uninformative.
- #2 and the pre-set rule: The pre-set rule rejects every capped arm (5-day cap: 17.6% late in Oct–Mar vs the 7% bar). Its own pick uses the 99th percentile in 7 of 11 months and lengthens promises by 7.5 days on average all year. Testing a capped cut is a judgement call that overrides the rule.
- Interactions: Rec 1 changes how lateness is recorded in stars, so the A/B runs after it ships, never across it. Rec 3 delays the recorded delivery, which delays the star survey and raises the measured late rate. Sizes are upper bounds and not additive.
- #1 bound: pre-delivery ratings get the score of same-bin post-delivery ratings; 61% of them sit in the 8+-day bins, where only 65 post-delivery reviews exist.
- Stage split: each stage's whole distribution is swapped (rank-preserving quantile mapping), Shapley over orderings; residual +0.6 pp.
- Strike IV: first-stage F 42 (purchase-day clusters), Anderson–Rubin set [-2.05, -0.9]. The post-delivery IV is INVALID (the strike shifts who answers after delivery).
- Review effects are bounds (post-delivery reviewers are selected); same-delivery-time conditions on a mediator; the RD at the promise fails and is shown only as a falsification exhibit.
- Promise policies: rolling backtest, no look-ahead, never-delivered = late, chosen on Oct-2017..Mar-2018. Conversion upside is NOT measured; Fisher, Gallino & Xu (2019) measured actual delivery speed.
- Text labels: keyword classifier vs single-annotator labels, misclassification-corrected.
- Not in the data: costs, margins, refunds, sessions, carrier IDs, Olist's targets. The extract may be a sample.
